metadata.title: Where Does Cold Dark Energy Switch On? A Precisely Posed Question at M >~ 10^12.4 Msun (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.0 draft (2026-10-27). DRAFT ONLY, NOT DEPOSITED. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

The programme studies a galaxy law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32 pi) (kappa = 1/2 fitted), with a gravitating w ~ 0 field component called cold dark energy (not matter, not a particle). The law fits isolated galaxies; groups and clusters need cold dark energy halos. The record's organising rule is environment-keyed: halos in satellites and in systems above a mass threshold. This note poses, from frozen and reproduced calculations, what the switch mechanism must do. (1) The threshold is not the core-floor crossover: one concentration c_f cannot set both the threshold and the group/cluster cores (no c_f in 3.5-6.0 passes every line); KiDS isolated-lens lensing needs a threshold >= 10^12.39 Msun (canonical) while groups need c_f >= 4.75. (2) Cluster outskirts need c_f >= 5.25 and cluster centres <= 5.0. (3) The outskirt deficit is not correlated structure beyond turnaround (changes outer predictions by at most 1.3%). (4) Below the threshold, the surviving exclusion mechanism (initial displacement, M6) is not yet decided by four native Lyman-alpha forest models; if the forest-side budget is real, galaxies needing it must retain at least 19-56% (canonical) / 28-83% (alternative) of their patch baryons. The question posed: what switches cold dark energy on at M >~ 10^12.4 Msun independently of halo concentration, and what sets the outer cluster budget separately from core concentration? No result here is evidence for the framework over LambdaCDM. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).
